### `.5.d.3` RE-PROFILE #3 (session #98, 2026-07-12) — the `.5.d.3` premise is FALSIFIED before building; toolbox-first, applying the `.5.d.2` lesson

**Why (the `.5.d.2` lesson, applied).** `.5.d.3`'s status line reads "the `.5.d.2` null proves the RE-PROFILE #2 ~70% clone/malloc is the MEMO deep-clones." That is an **inference**, not a measurement — and the durable `.5.d.2` lesson ([[project_lazy_winner_only_materialization_lesson]]) is *before landing a speed lever, MEASURE the marginal gain against the CURRENT baseline; do not infer*. So, per [[project_uvm_memory_not_the_memo]] ("profile, don't infer") + TOOLBOX-first, I profiled the memo-clone cost SPECIFICALLY **before** building the (high-risk, `'input`-lifetime × `Rc`/arena) `.5.d.3` change.

**Tool 1 — `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` (the memo footprint is tiny).** Over the 8 `regex_perf_probe` patterns (`parseability_probe --parse regex`, the eager/main `.5.c.2` baseline binary sha `449faa8b…`): the LARGEST memo footprint is character_class at **396 subtree-nodes across 218 success entries = avg 1.8 nodes/entry** (mostly `Terminal(&str)` leaves — a non-allocating pointer copy on clone). Biggest single memo entry ≈ 8 nodes (`descending_class_range`). anchor_complex 231 nodes / capture_groups 169 / email_basic 85. The clone-on-INSERT volume the memo pays is therefore small and cheap.

**Tool 2 — macOS `sample` (40 s @1 ms, 33,671 leaf samples, same binary), self-time buckets:**

| Bucket | Share | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **malloc + free + memops** | **54.6%** (malloc 24.4 / free 16.8 / memmove+memcmp+memset+bzero 13.4) | broad allocation of ALL parse structures (winner AST + serde_json Values + Vecs + Strings). Only the ARENA (mass allocation) + construction-elimination attacks this at the root. |
| parse work | 17.5% | the surviving branches' real work (`parse_atom`/`parse_piece`/`parse_letter`/`match_string`/`::new` closures) |
| drop | 6.9% | `drop_in_place<serde_json::Value>` 491 + BTreeMap `dying_next` 528 + `[ParseNode]`/`ParseNode`/`ParseContent` drops |
| semantic-runtime | 4.4% | `directives_for_rule` 503 + `rollback_to_named` 469 + `extract_delta_since` 151 |
| clone | 4.2% | BTreeMap `clone_subtree` 574 (**serde_json Value::Object**, ancestry = `to_json_value`/`parse_simple_escape`) + `Vec::clone` 323 + `ParseNode::clone` 291 + `ParseContent::clone` 137 |
| **`split_semantic_top_level`** | **2.8%** (930) | RE-SPLITTING the FIXED predicate-expression string on `||`/`&&`/6 comparison ops per predicate EVALUATION (`evaluate_relational_expression_inner`) — a pure repeated recomputation |
| hash | 1.7% | residual SipHash/hashbrown (memo) |
| probe timing | 1.5% | `mach_absolute_time` — the bench's per-parse clock reads, NOT parse cost |

**THE FINDING (decisive, tool-backed).** The `.5.d.3`-as-specified DIRECT target — `ParseNode::clone` (0.86%) + `ParseContent::clone` (0.41%) = **1.27% of self-time**, and only the memo-attributable FRACTION of that (most memo entries are `Terminal(&str)` leaves whose clone does not even allocate). This is the **same speed-neutral territory as `.5.d.2`** — well under the decisive-separation bar every landed lever cleared. The `.5.d.3` premise ("memo deep-clones are the single biggest clone source") is **FALSIFIED**: the biggest clone item is actually serde_json `Value::Object`/BTreeMap (the WINNER's return-annotation JSON transform, ancestry `to_json_value`), which `.5.d.3` does not touch. The real cost is **broad construction malloc (54.6%)**, fixable only by the ARENA + construction-elimination — i.e. the `.5.d.4` lockstep advance (piece 3), NOT standalone memo node-sharing.

**Consequence — `.5.d.3` (memo NODE sharing) alone is a predicted ~1% null**, exactly like `.5.d.2`; its real value is as a COMPOSING PIECE of `.5.d.4` (where the arena/Rc handle + the lockstep advance together eliminate the 54.6% at the root). This mirrors `.5.d.2` (lazy materialization → folded into `.5.d.4`). Two profile-indicated levers now stand out:
- **The arena / `.5.d.4` lockstep advance** — the agreed destination's core; the ONLY thing that moves the 54.6% construction malloc. Big + high-risk (R-a..R-d).
- **Predicate-expression PRECOMPILE** (NEW, off the `.5.d` sequence) — parse the FIXED relational predicate expression to an AST ONCE (at annotation-compile time) and evaluate the AST, instead of re-splitting the string on every evaluation. Attacks `split_semantic_top_level` 2.8% + the surrounding `evaluate_relational_expression_inner` re-parse cascade + its Vec malloc. Byte-identical (same split result), low-risk, parser-agnostic (every predicate-using grammar inherits it). A clean bankable win while `.5.d.4` is designed.

**⛔ DECISION SURFACED to the director, NOT decided unilaterally** ([[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]] — the anti-drift + UNFORESEEN-ISSUE protocol: a queued leaf's premise falsified by a fresh profile changes the agreed next step, so PAUSE → analyze → propose → AGREE, before acting). Options surfaced: (A, recommended) advance to `.5.d.4` (fold `.5.d.3`/`.5.d.2` in as pieces) — the agreed core, the only 54.6% lever; (B) bank the byte-identical predicate-precompile detour first, then `.5.d.4`; (C) build `.5.d.3` arena/Rc scaffolding as a standalone step anyway (predicted ~1% null, but it is the `.5.d.4` foundation). Raw data: session scratchpad `sample_memo.txt`. Docs-only steering slice — no code change.

### `.5.d.4` DESIGN (session #98, 2026-07-12) — the lockstep DFA advance: machinery survey + R-a resolution + increment decomposition

**Decision context.** RE-PROFILE #3 falsified the standalone `.5.d.3` premise (memo node-clone = 1.27%); the director chose **option A** — advance to `.5.d.4` (the lockstep DFA advance + arena), the ONLY lever that moves the dominant 54.6% construction malloc, folding `.5.d.3` (memo sharing) and `.5.d.2` (lazy winner-only materialization) in as composing pieces. Docs-first design (NO code); the code increment is gated on the R-a agreement below (a pre-registered pause-and-agree point).

**Machinery survey (tool-grounded — `ast_based_generator.rs` `generate_or_logic`, verified line refs against the main/`.5.c.2` baseline).** The multi-branch tournament (`generate_or_logic`, `:3495`) is a SERIAL try-each:
- `parse_start = parser.position` (`:4024`); `best_end = parse_start`, `best_content/best_raw_content = None`, `best_priority = i64::MIN`, `best_branch_index/best_branch = 0`, `nonassoc_tie = false` (`:4024`–`:4031`).
- For each branch `idx` (via a `match idx { … }` over `branch_attempt_arms`, each optionally wrapped in the `.5.c.2` first-set prune guard `:3976`): `parser.position = parse_start` (`:3710`), `try_parse` the branch body (`:3711`), and on success capture `candidate_end = parser.position` (`:3722`), `raw_content` (`:3725`), run the return-annotation transform BEFORE rollback (`:3735`, BRANCH-BROADCAST-FIX.3 for `$text`), `parser.position = parse_start` (`:3739`), evaluate branch `@predicate`s (`:3742`), extract the C3-B `SemanticRuntimeDelta` (`:3927`), then `should_take` (`:3865`–`:3913`) decides via longest-match (`candidate_end > best_end`) with priority/`@associativity` tie-break (`right` → later branch wins; `nonassoc` equal-priority tie → `nonassoc_tie=true`). If `should_take`: update `best_end/best_content/best_branch_index/best_branch/best_semantic_delta`.
- After all branches: if `nonassoc_tie` → `Err(Backtrack)` (`:4069`); else `parser.position = best_end` (`:4074`), emit the `🏁 selected branch` trace, apply the winner's delta once (`apply_delta`, `:4098`), apply the winner's branch-start inline effects (`:4006`), return the winner's content. Cost = O(Σ branch-cost) with a full rollback per branch — the serial-try waste `.5.d.4` eliminates.

**R-a — furthest_position preservation (RESOLVED; the make-or-break correctness risk).** TOOL-VERIFIED FACT: `furthest_position` is written at EXACTLY ONE site — rule-method entry (`ast_based_generator.rs:3288` `if self.position > self.furthest_position { self.furthest_position = self.position }`; ALL 274 sites in `generated/regex_parser.rs` are that identical pattern; `match_string`/terminal matching NEVER write it; the interpreter mirrors it at `parse_harness_interpreter.rs:851`). It is monotone and never rolled back on speculation. Consequences for the lockstep advance:
- A **terminal branch** (regex `atom` alternative like `\d`, `\w`, a class shorthand, a literal) enters NO nested rule method, so its ONLY furthest contribution is the Or-rule's own entry = `parse_start` — already recorded before the tournament. A multi-char terminal that matches k chars then mismatches does NOT bump furthest beyond `parse_start` (match_string never writes it). ⇒ terminal branches are **furthest-neutral by construction** — the exact `.5.c.2` soundness argument (`:3983` "pruning is furthest_position-neutral, the rule entry already recorded parse_start").
- A **group-family branch** (`group`/`lookaround`/… all share the `(` introducer, discriminated by a deterministic longer prefix `(?:`/`(?P<`/`(?=`/`(?!`/`(`) : at a given position at most one prefix matches; the lockstep discriminates it and RECURSES into that branch via normal recursive-descent (which enters the nested rules and bumps furthest EXACTLY as today), while the non-matching group branches fail SHALLOW at the prefix (furthest ≤ prefix mismatch) — the same shallow reach the serial try gives them. ⇒ furthest preserved in both the recursive part (unchanged) and the discrimination part (shallow, ≤ serial).
- **Backstop:** `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` asserts byte-level `furthest_position` equality (interp[serial] vs generated[lockstep], ALL grammars, seeds 0/7/42) + `parse_harness_combinator_gate` covers the `a|ab` longest-match discrimination — so any lost furthest bump FAILS the gate. R-a is furthest-neutral by the verified single-write invariant AND oracle-checked.

**R-a AGREEMENT ASK (pre-registered pause-and-agree, [[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]]).** The R-a resolution above (furthest-neutral by the single rule-entry write + deterministic prefix discrimination + the equivalence-gate furthest backstop) is the proposed solution for the pre-registered R-a risk. Surfaced for the director's agreement BEFORE the first `.5.d.4` code increment. **→ ✅ AGREED (director, session #99, 2026-07-12, AskUserQuestion): "Greenlight — start increment (i) now."**

**Capability gate (parser-agnostic, CAPABILITY not grammar-name — [[feedback_features_parser_agnostic_enable_all_parsers]]).** The lockstep advance applies to a choice site whose branches are DFA-discriminable: each branch is (a) a pure terminal/regular sequence, or (b) a terminal-prefix-then-recurse form where the shared introducer is discriminated deterministically and the recursion runs as normal recursive-descent. Excluded (stay serial): branches with a branch-phase `@predicate` whose liveness depends on the store (F5c precision 3 — they stay live until the predicate resolves), and branches whose furthest contribution is NOT ≤ their discrimination point (non-prefix-disjoint recursive branches). The gate is a codegen capability check on the branch set, emitted per choice site; a site that fails the gate keeps today's byte-identical serial tournament.

**R-d (arena × `'input` lifetime) — DESIGN NEXT (not yet resolved).** The winner's AST is built once into an arena freed en masse; the memo returns a shared handle (`.5.d.3` folded in). The open question is the ownership/lifetime shape: `ParseNode<'input>` borrows the input; an arena/`Rc` handle must coexist with `'input`. Candidate: an arena keyed to the parse (dropped with the parser), nodes as arena indices or `&'arena`-borrowed, with `'arena: 'input` or a two-lifetime `ParseNode<'input, 'arena>`. This is the next design increment (R-d is its own pre-registered pause-and-agree point).

**Increment decomposition (each: design → decisive drift-controlled `regex_perf_probe` before→after → full ⛔ HARD-CONSTRAINT oracle battery → land iff faster + byte-identical).** (i) the terminal-only lockstep advance for the `atom` choice (the biggest, simplest DFA-discriminable site; folds in lazy winner-only materialization since a lockstep advance cannot transform per-branch) — measures the win from eliminating serial try + rollback on the hottest site; (ii) extend to group-family prefix discrimination; (iii) the arena + memo sharing (R-d) — the piece that attacks the 54.6% construction malloc at the root; (iv) generalize the capability gate across choice sites. Sequenced smallest-risk-first; each independently measurable so a null (like `.5.d.2`/`.5.d.3`) is caught before the next. The three F5c precisions (longest-match winner, lazy AST/effects, store-gated liveness) are preserved by every increment; the oracle is the `parse_harness_*` byte-identical differential + the full battery.

### `.5.d.4` R-d DESIGN (session #99, 2026-07-12) — arena × `'input` lifetime: ownership-model survey + recommendation + the pre-registered pause-and-agree

**Why now (plan-adherent, docs-only).** MEMORY next_action sequenced this: agree R-a → **design R-d** → first code increment. R-d is the second pre-registered pause-and-agree point (the tree's UNFORESEEN-ISSUE PROTOCOL). Designing it now — like `-0019` designed R-a — lets both pause points be surfaced for a single combined director agreement, so the whole `.5.d.4` road is greenlit as a unit before any code. NO code change here (design only).

**The two deep-clone sites R-d must eliminate (TOOL-VERIFIED, `ast_based_generator.rs` `memoized_call`).** (1) clone-on-INSERT `:7185` — `MemoEntry { result: Some(node.clone()), raw_semantic_content: raw_semantic_content.clone(), … }` deep-clones the whole `ParseNode<'input>` subtree into the memo on every success; (2) clone-on-HIT `:7130` — `return Ok((node.clone(), entry.raw_semantic_content.clone()))` deep-clones it back OUT on every cache hit. `ParseNode::clone` recurses through `ParseContent` (`mod.rs:715`): `Sequence(Vec<ParseNode>)` / `Alternative(Box<ParseNode>)` / `Quantified(Vec<ParseNode>)` deep-copy their children; `Json(serde_json::Value)` clones the map; only `Terminal(&'input str)` is a cheap pointer copy. RE-PROFILE #3 measured the memo-clone FRACTION at 1.27% — so R-d's real prize is NOT the memo clone per se but the **54.6% broad construction malloc** the arena attacks (bulk-alloc all nodes + mass-free losers), with memo sharing (`.5.d.3`) folded in as the cheap by-product.

**The `'input` borrow (the constraint that makes this non-trivial).** `ParseContent::Terminal(&'input str)` means the parse tree BORROWS the input, which outlives the parse. Any arena/handle scheme MUST preserve that borrow — this is the "coexist with `'input`" crux R-d flags.

**Blast radius (TOOL-VERIFIED) — and why it is SMALLER than it looks.** `ParseNode`/`ParseContent` are referenced across **~22 source files** (`grep -rln`). BUT the **public/crate boundary returns OWNED data, never a borrowed tree**: `parser_registry::parse_sample_ast_json*` → `serde_json::Value`; `embedding_api` → `Result<String,…>` (serialized). The tree is walked to owned JSON at the boundary via `ParseContent::to_json_value` (`mod.rs:731`) and the arena/tree is dropped. ⇒ `ParseNode<'input>` NEVER escapes borrowed to a consumer, so an arena (or even a second lifetime) is confined to the **internal parse machinery + the one boundary serialize walk** — the public API is UNCHANGED by construction. This de-risks the whole change. (Also TOOL-VERIFIED: no arena crate — `bumpalo`/`typed-arena`/`id-arena`/`slotmap` — is in `Cargo.toml` today.)

**Three candidate ownership models (each weighed against: moves the 54.6%? · `'input` coexistence · blast radius · new dep · folds `.5.d.3`?).**

- **(A) `Rc<ParseNode<'input>>` shared handles — single lifetime, ref-counted sharing.** Memo stores `Rc<ParseNode<'input>>`: insert = one `Rc::new`, hit = `Rc::clone` (pointer + refcount bump, ZERO deep-clone). Optionally children become `Rc` for true subtree sharing. **Moves 54.6%? NO** — still one heap alloc PER node (`Rc::new`), no bulk-alloc, no mass-free; it only removes the memo re-clone. **`'input`:** trivial (single lifetime preserved). **Blast radius:** small. **New dep:** none. **Folds `.5.d.3`:** yes (that IS `.5.d.3`). **Verdict:** a clean low-risk SHARING primitive but INSUFFICIENT ALONE for the dominant cost — predicted ~1% (exactly the RE-PROFILE #3 finding for standalone `.5.d.3`). Value = a composing piece, not the lever.

- **(B) Bump arena + `&'arena` borrows — two lifetimes `ParseNode<'input, 'arena>`, `'arena: 'input`.** A `bumpalo`-style arena tied to the parse; nodes are `&'arena ParseNode<'input, 'arena>`; the winner is walked to owned JSON at the boundary, then the arena is dropped (losers freed EN MASSE — one free, not K). **Moves 54.6%? YES** — bulk alloc + mass-free, the actual lever. **`'input`:** needs the `'arena: 'input` outlives-bound + a self-referential `&'arena ParseNode<'input,'arena>` (the classic arena-of-self pattern). **Blast radius:** TWO lifetimes propagate across the internal machinery (~22 files' internal uses) — but NOT the public API (owned boundary). **New dep:** `bumpalo`. **Folds `.5.d.3`:** yes (memo stores `&'arena ParseNode`, hit returns the shared borrow).

- **(C) Plain-`Vec` arena + `NodeId(u32)` indices — single `'input` lifetime, indices not borrows. ★ RECOMMENDED.** All nodes live in one `Vec<ParseNode<'input>>` arena; children are referenced by a `NodeId(u32)` index (`Sequence(Vec<NodeId>)`, `Alternative(NodeId)`, `Quantified(Vec<NodeId>)`) instead of `Box`/`Vec<ParseNode>`. Memo stores a `NodeId` + `end_pos`; a hit returns the `NodeId` (a `Copy` — ZERO clone). The arena is one growable Vec (bulk alloc via doubling), dropped at parse end (mass free); contiguous layout is cache-friendly (the simdjson tape idea). **Moves 54.6%? YES** — same bulk-alloc + mass-free as B. **`'input`:** stays a SINGLE lifetime — indices are `u32`, so no second lifetime and no self-referential borrow; the arena `Vec<ParseNode<'input>>` simply holds the same `'input` borrow the tree always had. **Blast radius:** every tree-WALKER (`to_json_value` `mod.rs:731`, the return-transform `ast_return_transform.rs`, the interpreter `parse_harness_interpreter.rs:*`, the AST-shape dumper) must thread the arena `&[ParseNode]` to resolve `NodeId` — a mechanical, contained refactor (no lifetime virality). **New dep:** NONE. **Folds `.5.d.3`:** yes (memo stores a `NodeId`, hit is a Copy).

**RECOMMENDATION — Candidate C.** It delivers the same bulk-allocation + mass-free that moves the dominant 54.6% construction malloc as B, AND folds in `.5.d.3` memo sharing (memo → `NodeId`, hit is a Copy), while keeping the SINGLE `'input` lifetime — avoiding B's viral two-lifetime `ParseNode<'input,'arena>` propagation and adding NO new dependency. The price is threading the arena slice through the handful of tree-walkers to resolve `NodeId`, which is mechanical and confined (vs a lifetime that infects every internal `ParseNode` signature). The public boundary is unchanged (walk to owned `serde_json::Value`, drop arena). Byte-identical by construction: the tree is structurally identical, merely referenced by index instead of `Box`/`Vec` — the boundary JSON is the same bytes, proven by the `parse_harness_*` differential (verdict + AST + `furthest_position`, all grammars, seeds 0/7/42) + the PCRE2 per-case diff + the all-parsers byte-identical regen. (If C's walker-threading proves unexpectedly heavy in practice, B is the fallback — same performance envelope, lifetime cost instead of index-threading cost; A is retained only as the `.5.d.3` sharing sub-step if we ever want memo sharing WITHOUT the arena.)

**Sequencing (important — R-d is increment (iii), not (i)).** The FIRST code increment (i) — the terminal-only lockstep advance for `atom` — does NOT need the arena; it eliminates serial try + rollback and folds in lazy materialization, measurable on its own. The arena (R-d) lands at increment (iii), the piece that attacks the 54.6% at the root. So R-d is agreed **in principle NOW** (greenlight the arena DIRECTION — candidate C — for the road), with the concrete arena code deferred to increment (iii) after (i)/(ii) measure the lockstep win. Both R-a and R-d are surfaced before ANY code precisely so the director greenlights the whole `.5.d.4` shape as a unit (the pre-registered pause-and-agree discipline).

**R-d AGREEMENT ASK (pre-registered pause-and-agree, [[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]]).** Recommend **candidate C** (plain-`Vec` arena + `NodeId(u32)` indices, single `'input` lifetime, no new dep) as the arena ownership model for increment (iii); B (two-lifetime `&'arena`) is the fallback, A (`Rc`-only) is insufficient alone. Surfaced for the director's agreement (direction only; the arena code is increment (iii), after increment (i)) alongside the R-a resolution, BEFORE the first `.5.d.4` code increment. **→ ✅ AGREED: candidate C (director, session #99, 2026-07-12, AskUserQuestion). B is the fallback if C's index-threading proves heavy; the arena code lands at increment (iii).**

### `.5.d.4.i` — CODE INCREMENT (i): terminal-only lockstep advance for the `atom` choice (session #99, 2026-07-12) — director-AGREED, IN PROGRESS

**Scope (the smallest, safest first increment).** Replace the SERIAL try-each-branch tournament with a lockstep forward scan ONLY for the `atom` choice site (regex.ebnf:365, the hottest DFA-discriminable site) and ONLY its terminal-family branches; folds in lazy winner-only materialization (a lockstep advance cannot transform per-branch). Every other choice site + any non-terminal `atom` branch keeps today's byte-identical serial tournament (the capability gate). Parser-agnostic codegen (`generate_or_logic`), gated on CAPABILITY not grammar-name. NO arena yet (that is increment (iii), R-d candidate C) — increment (i) measures the win from eliminating serial-try + rollback alone.

**⚠️ PRE-REGISTERED risk to watch (the `.5.d.2`/`.5.d.3` pattern).** `.5.c.2` first-set dispatch already prunes most losing branches before they are tried, so the serial-try + rollback overhead increment (i) removes may already be small ⇒ increment (i) alone COULD be a null (like `.5.d.2`/`.5.d.3`), with the real 54.6%-construction-malloc win coming at increment (iii) (the arena) that this restructuring enables. Per the decomposition this is measured EXPLICITLY: if increment (i) is byte-identical-but-neutral, it does NOT land standalone (HARD CONSTRAINT) — the lockstep restructuring is then re-introduced combined with the arena at (iii), exactly as lazy materialization (`.5.d.2`) is re-introduced here. A null is DATA, caught before (iii). If a genuinely unforeseen issue surfaces mid-implementation → PAUSE + analyze + agree (UNFORESEEN-ISSUE PROTOCOL).

#### ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (session #99, before building — the `.5.d.3` precedent: predict the marginal gain from the profile FIRST)

Increment (i)'s acceptance checklist begins with REPRODUCE + ROOT CAUSE the cost it removes. Doing that against the committed RE-PROFILE #3 profile (33,671 leaf samples on the current on-disk eager `.5.c.2` baseline) BEFORE building — exactly the `.5.d.3` method ("profile the target cost specifically before the invasive change"):

- A TERMINAL-ONLY lockstep advance removes the SERIAL try-each per-branch **backtrack** cost: `rollback_to_named` (469 samples) + `extract_delta_since` (151) = **620 samples = 1.84% of self-time**. `directives_for_rule` (503 = 1.49%) is NOT removed (the lockstep still consults per-rule directives). Folding in lazy winner-only materialization adds **≈0** — `.5.d.2` already MEASURED lazy-vs-eager as a null (because `.5.c.2` first-set dispatch prunes the losing branches before they are tried/transformed).

#### ✅ ARENA MODEL DECISION (session #100, 2026-07-12) — candidate C CONFIRMED (C-vs-B re-weighed pre-code, tool-backed; the Drop-correctness decider)

**Context.** Before writing a line of the phase's riskiest byte-identity change, a tool-backed scoping pass re-weighed the C-vs-B choice the director made in session #99. Two findings changed the picture; the director then delegated the call ("you are the expert coder — pick the SOTA, signoff, most durable, clean, rock-solid approach and roll"). Decision: **candidate C, on firmer Drop-aware footing.**

**Finding 1 — the type change is SINGLE-SITE (shrinks the surgery).** TOOL-VERIFIED the generated parsers `use crate::ast_pipeline::{… ParseContent, ParseNode, MemoEntry, …}` (`generated/regex_parser.rs:3`) — they do NOT define their own copy. So `ParseContent`/`ParseNode`/`MemoEntry` live in exactly ONE place (`mod.rs`); the blueprint's "two copies in lockstep" worry is void. `ast_code_generator.rs` (its inert `quote!` template with a simpler `ParseContent`) is legacy/uninvoked (no `AstCodeGenerator::new` outside its own file) — leave it alone.

**Finding 2 — the crux the blueprint mislabeled "mechanical."** `ast_return_transform.rs` (the return-annotation codegen — historically the most byte-identity-fragile area: PGEN-RGX-0075/0077, the `<invalid_sequence_access>` sentinels) EMITS runtime code that treats `ParseContent` children as OWNED, MOVABLE values: `for node in nodes { array_elements.push(node) }` (moves children out of `Sequence`/`Quantified`), `elements[N].content.clone()` (owned index), `while let Alternative(node) = current { current = node.content }` (peel by move), and mid-transform `ParseNode { rule_name, content: …, span }` CONSTRUCTION (spread/flatten-spread wrappers). ~15 such emitted sites (`grep` verified: lines 174/176/191/223-233/284-339/424-436/501/559-562/615-627/671/851). Under C (`Vec<NodeId>` children on a `self.arena`) these are NOT a mechanical `arena[id]` swap — a fresh wrapper must be `arena.push`'d (`&mut`) while the same loop reads `arena[child]` (`&`) — a borrow interleave to hand-resolve byte-identically, in the fragile codegen.

**The C-vs-B re-weigh + the decider (Drop-correctness).** `ParseContent` carries `String` (`TransformedTerminal`) and `serde_json::Value` (`Json`) — heap-owning `Drop` types. Any arena MUST run their destructors or LEAK on every parse:
- **C (`Vec<ParseNode>` + `NodeId`)** — Drop-correct FOR FREE (the `Vec` drops every element). Single `'input` lifetime. No dep. Memo stores a `NodeId` (Copy) ⇒ folds `.5.d.3` sharing. ✅
- **B / plain `bumpalo`** — `Bump` does NOT run `Drop` ⇒ leaks every `String`/`Value` in the tree, unbounded. ✗ DISQUALIFIED (a hazard the session-#99 surface under-weighted; `bumpalo` is transitively in `Cargo.lock:98` but is NOT a direct pgen dep).
- **B / `typed-arena` (the Drop-correct ref-arena, rustc `TypedArena` shape)** — works, but adds a dep AND the viral `'arena` second lifetime.

**Durability decider (the director's stated criterion).** `ParseContent`/`ParseNode` is a CORE type touched by 13 files. A viral `'arena` lifetime (`ParseNode<'input,'arena>`) is a PERMANENT signature tax across all of them, complicating every future change. **rust-analyzer** — a large, long-lived, signoff-grade codebase — deliberately chose INDEX arenas (`la_arena::Idx`) over reference arenas for its syntax trees for exactly this reason (no lifetime virality, simpler signatures, serializable). Strong SOTA precedent that the single-lifetime index arena is the cleaner, more durable choice for a large tree-heavy codebase. The public boundary is already owned (`serde_json::Value`), so C's arena is a purely internal detail either way.

**⇒ DECISION (SUPERSEDED — see the REVISION below): candidate C** — Drop-correct by construction, single `'input` lifetime (no viral tax), no naive-bumpalo leak, `la_arena`-grade precedent, folds `.5.d.3` memo sharing. The transform crux is handled with a disciplined **read-then-push** borrow pattern. This conclusion was REVERSED within the same session by a second tool-backed finding (below); the Findings 1/2 + the Drop-correctness analysis above remain valid and inform candidate B too.

#### 🔁 ARENA MODEL DECISION — REVISED to candidate B (session #100, 2026-07-12, director-confirmed) — the derived-`Serialize` oracle is the decider

**The finding that reversed C→B (tool-backed).** The authoritative typed-AST — the exact bytes EVERY differential gate compares (`parse_harness_equivalence` asserts `interp.ast_json == oracle_value`) and `parse_sample_ast_json` returns — is **`serde_json::to_value(&ParseNode)` via `#[derive(Serialize)]`**, at THREE boundary sites: `parser_registry.rs:1083` (`parse_node_to_json`), `parse_harness_interpreter.rs:416`, `parse_harness.rs:457`. NOT `to_json_value` (which is a SEPARATE return-transform-internal path). Consequence:
- **Candidate C (`Sequence(Vec<NodeId>)`) BREAKS the oracle** — the derive would emit BARE INDICES (`{"Sequence":[0,5,12]}`) instead of the nested subtree, and `serde::Serialize::serialize(&self, S)` has NO channel to receive the arena to resolve them. C would force a hand-written, byte-PERFECT reimplementation of serde's externally-tagged derive (enum tagging, `Range`→`{start,end}`, `Quantified` tuple-as-array) — i.e. reproducing THE ORACLE ITSELF by hand. The single most byte-identity-dangerous change possible; directly threatens the #1 immovable correctness floor.
- **Candidate B (`&'arena` references) PRESERVES the oracle FOR FREE** — serde serializes `&T`/`&[T]` byte-identically to `T`, so `#[derive(Serialize)]` on `ParseNode<'input,'arena>` with `Alternative(&'arena ParseNode)`/`Sequence(&'arena [ParseNode])` produces the SAME bytes as today's `Box`/`Vec`. The fragile return-transform code barely changes (children stay dereferenceable; `for node in nodes` still works; construction is `arena.alloc(...)` with no `&mut`/`&` borrow interleave since the arena hands out `&'arena` via interior mutability).

**Drop-correctness (resolved for B).** `ParseContent` carries `String`+`serde_json::Value` (heap `Drop`). Plain `bumpalo` (the only vendored arena, `Cargo.lock:98`) does NOT run `Drop` ⇒ would leak every parse ✗. **`typed-arena`** (small, standard, zero-transitive-deps, the rustc `TypedArena` shape) IS Drop-correct (runs destructors on arena drop) AND hands out `&'arena mut T` from `&self` (build children-then-parents; parents reference children). So B = `typed_arena::Arena<ParseNode<'input,'arena>>`, created at the boundary, passed as `&'arena Arena` to the parser (NOT owned by it ⇒ no self-referential struct), dropped after the boundary serialize walk = mass-free. Memo stores `Option<&'arena ParseNode>` (Copy) ⇒ folds `.5.d.3` sharing for free.

**Cost of B (accepted):** a viral `'arena` second lifetime on `ParseNode`/`ParseContent`/`MemoEntry` and every internal signature touching them — mechanical, COMPILER-CHECKED (a slip is a compile error, never a silent byte diff), and INTERNAL-ONLY (the public boundary returns owned `serde_json::Value`, so `'arena` never leaks to consumers) — plus one new direct dep (`typed-arena`).

**⇒ DECISION: candidate B via `typed-arena`** (director-confirmed, session #100, AskUserQuestion: "B via typed-arena dep (recommended)"). Rationale honors the director's stated criteria (SOTA/signoff/durable/clean/ROCK-SOLID) with correctness-floor primacy: B keeps the byte-identity oracle intact by construction (the dominant consideration), vs C reproducing the oracle by hand. The viral lifetime is the price, paid in compiler-checked mechanical churn, not byte-identity risk. Byte-identity still gated CHEAPLY by the debug oracles before any fat-LTO.

**Revised migration order (candidate B):** (1) add `typed-arena` dep; (2) `mod.rs` — `ParseContent<'input,'arena>`/`ParseNode<'input,'arena>`/`MemoEntry<'input,'arena>` with `&'arena` children + the `'arena` lifetime; `to_json_value` needs NO arena param (children are refs); (3) interpreter (`parse_harness_interpreter.rs`) — build into an `Arena`, mirror the lifetime; (4) codegen (`ast_based_generator.rs`) — the parser struct gains `arena: &'arena Arena<ParseNode<'input,'arena>>`, construction sites `self.arena.alloc(ParseNode{...})`, rule methods return `&'arena ParseNode`, memo stores the ref; (5) thread `'arena` through the walkers until it compiles (mostly signature churn, bodies unchanged); (6) regen 11 parsers + debug oracles (equivalence/combinator/semantic) + fat-LTO measure. Boundary sites (`parse_node_to_json` etc.) create the `Arena` and pass it in. Land iff faster + byte-identical.

#### B. Literature survey (the research-grounded GLL adjudication)

- **GLL** [Scott & Johnson, *GLL Parsing*, ENTCS 253(7) 2010]: generalizes RD to ALL CFGs via descriptors + a graph-structured
  stack (GSS); O(n³) worst case. Its value = handling nondeterminism/ambiguity that would make plain RD exponential or incorrect.
- **Optimized GLL** [Afroozeh & Izmaylova, *Faster, Practical GLL Parsing*, CC 2015 (Iguana)]: a more efficient GSS + optimizations,
  evaluated on highly-ambiguous + real programming-language grammars — the strongest practical GLL.
- **The decisive comparison** [Parr, Harwell, Fisher, *Adaptive LL(\*) Parsing: The Power of Dynamic Analysis*, OOPSLA 2014]:
  ALL(*) — top-down parsing with adaptive lookahead-DFA-cached prediction — "**outperforms general strategies such as GLL and GLR
  by orders of magnitude**" on grammars used in practice (e.g. 3.2MB Java in 360ms vs GLL/GLR-family tools needing GBs + far longer;
  their own data shows the prediction CACHE is what makes it viable — uncached simulation is 100–1000× slower).
- **Worked mapping to PGEN.** Post-`.5.c.2`, PGEN's engine already occupies the ALL(*)-side of this divide: memoized (packrat)
  recursive descent + STATIC k=1 first-set pruning + delta-based winner-only store effects. The regex grammar is deterministic
  (tournament winner selection, no ambiguity — a true `(rule,start,end)` SPPF has nothing to share); the surviving-branch sets after
  first-set pruning are singleton-or-small. GLL's machinery would REPLACE cheap native call/return with heap-allocated descriptors +
  GSS node/edge bookkeeping + SPPF construction on EVERY rule entry — i.e., it ADDS a per-entry constant to the exact ~262ns/entry
  floor that IS the problem, in exchange for removing a backtrack residue measured at **~2.2%** (`rollback_to_named` 1.30% +
  `extract_delta_since` 0.85%). Even the adjacent within-family upgrade (ALL(*)-style adaptive k>1 prediction caching) targets only
  the residual failing probes (~38% of entries on `test` fail, but each fails at char 1 — already first-char-cheap).
- **VERDICT: REFUTED.** Predicted net-NEGATIVE (bookkeeping added ≫ residue removed), against a ≤3% honest ceiling; it cannot land
  under the ⛔ HARD CONSTRAINT (land iff faster + byte-identical). Same adjudication class as `.5.d.3` (premise falsified before
  building — the doctrine working as designed, zero trial-and-revert cost).

#### C. Road-level steering (SURFACED to the director — no unilateral re-sequencing; [[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]])

The agreed road said "`.5.g` then `.5.e`"; `.5.e`'s spike is complete and its premise is refuted, which puts the ROAD itself at a
decision point: **no remaining `.5` bucket lever can reach the `<5×` destination — the residual ≈20× is architectural.** The three
honest options (any combination):

1. **`.7` PARSE-CACHE + BATCH (recommended next).** Already queued, director-originated. The real RGX workload recompiles repeated
   patterns; a persistent pattern→AST cache makes the amortized per-pattern cost ≈0 (a cache hit is a hash + clone — plausibly
   ~1µs-scale, i.e. UNDER the 5× bound on the workload metric). Prerequisite either way: **vendor `pgen_iteration_flow`** so `.6`'s
   OFFICIAL corpus metric exists (this spike's 99× is the 8-pattern preview). Low risk, measurable, workload-honest.
2. **CASCADE FUSION / grammar-derived scanner compilation (the honest research-grade REPLACEMENT for GLL).** Attack the
   entries-per-char product directly: codegen-fuse LINEAR single-alternative wrapper chains (e.g. `literal→literal_char→letter`)
   and/or compile token-shaped regular sublanguages into direct-coded scanners that emit the identical arena nodes + typed JSON
   (byte-identical oracle unchanged). Ceiling if entries/char drop ~11→~2: ~3–5× on the bench — REAL but still short of 20× alone;
   sequence AFTER `.7` if the raw-latency race is still on once the workload metric exists. STEP-0 gate before any build: a
   fusibility census (count rule entries on the bench corpus that sit on single-alt chains / token-shaped rules).
3. **RE-BASELINE the `.6` closure bound (director decision).** `<5×` RAW vs a hand-written single-pass C compiler that emits no
   AST may be the wrong contract for a general grammar-driven parser emitting a typed JSON AST through annotations; candidate
   honest form: cache-amortized `<5×` on the real RGX iteration workload + a raw per-parse budget (e.g. geomean ≤ N µs).

**Recommendation: 1 → then adjudicate 2/3 with the official metric in hand.** Destination intent (make PGEN-regex fast enough that
speed is a non-issue for RGX) unchanged; this is a route correction surfaced BEFORE any action, per the standing discipline.

#### D. The DERIVED-SCANNER design sketch (director Q&A, session #105, 2026-07-13 — pre-decision, recorded so it survives; NO leaf opened)

Answering the director's "PGEN has no lexer/tokenizer — can we keep EBNF as sole source of truth, stay 100% parser-neutral, AND
benefit from a lexer+tokenizer?" — **YES, by DERIVING the scanner from the grammar, never declaring one**:

- **WHAT'S WRONG with the current model:** the full general-parser apparatus (memo probe + observability + semantic-runtime wrapper +
  tournament + node build + furthest tracking ≈ 262ns) is paid PER RULE ENTRY, and entries go down to single characters (~11/char on
  the bench) — finite-state recognition executed through a general rule engine at ~100× its intrinsic cost.
- **THE FAST SHAPE (layered execution, one grammar):** bottom layer = the grammar's REGULAR subtrees compiled to direct-coded DFAs
  (re2c/Ragel form, ~ns/char, no memo — linearity holds by construction); top layer = structural/annotated/store-gated rules keep the
  existing RD machinery but consume TOKENS ⇒ rule-entry cost per token, not per char.
- **THE CAPABILITY GATE (static, over the gen-AST — parser-AGNOSTIC, never name-gated):** a subtree is scanner-compilable iff
  (1) regular (no ref cycles; iteration via quantifiers only); (2) no outcome/store-affecting directives inside; (3) AST contribution
  reconstructible from matched text (increment 1 = only text-folding token rules — strictest); (4) choice semantics DFA-encodable —
  `longest_match` IS maximal munch (accept-state branch tagging; `a|ab` identical), `ordered`/`priority` = accept-priority tie-break;
  (5) grammar-declared layout policy respected at the boundary. NOT a pre-pass: each scanner is invoked exactly where the cascade
  would have been ⇒ context-dependent tokenization (the reason PGEN is scannerless) preserved BY CONSTRUCTION.
- **DUALITY untouched** (execution-only change; stimuli generation walks the same EBNF). **Pre-registered risks (pause-and-agree):**
  (R-i) rule-participation TESTIMONY must be synthesized by the fused scanner (cert coverage + contract gates consume it);
  (R-ii) furthest_position parity on rejection; (R-iii) gate breadth per grammar unknown until the census.
- **ROAD (the proven method):** STEP 0 = mechanical FUSIBILITY CENSUS over all shipped grammars (the ceiling, measured BEFORE any
  build — the `.5.d.3`/`.5.e` discipline) → DFA construction (Thompson/subset over the gen-AST; FIRST-set machinery already computes
  on this IR) → codegen emission (identical folded AST + testimony + furthest) → byte-identical increments (leaves → chains →
  keyword/alternation sets → deeper), interpreter stays UNFUSED as the fresh-walking reference oracle (the `.5.g` pointed-oracle
  pattern). Literature anchors for the spike: re2c/Ragel/flex (derived direct-coded scanners); context-aware scanning
  [Van Wyk & Schwerdfeger, Copper] (parser-context-informed lexing); ANTLR (derived lexer ATNs).
- **Honest ceiling:** ~70–80% fused entries ⇒ ~3–5× on the bench (→ ~12–19µs); raw `<5×` vs PCRE2 on FIRST-SEEN patterns remains
  uncertain ⇒ COMPOSES WITH (does not replace) `.7` parse-cache for the workload goal. SV/VHDL/JSON likely gain MORE than regex
  (multi-char tokens). This sketch = the concrete form of steering option (2); the road pick remains PENDING with the director.
- **DIRECTOR REQUIREMENT (stated 2026-07-13, session #105 — the design's acceptance frame):** *"keep the sole source of truth +
  return annotation + semantic annotation and still use a lexer and tokenizer in the background"* — satisfied by construction:
  the author-facing contract (one `.ebnf`, return + semantic annotations) is UNCHANGED; the scanner is a codegen-computed
  execution strategy (like FIRST sets / LR elimination), invisible to authors. Semantic-annotated/store-gated rules are excluded
  from fusion by the gate and run on the full runtime; token-shaped text-folding return annotations are applied by the scanner to
  the same matched text (byte-identical). The boundary is ADAPTIVE: adding a directive to a fused rule automatically un-fuses that
  subtree at the next regeneration — the grammar's own properties manage the lexer, never the author.

#### E. BRAINSTORM REGISTER (director + engineer, session #105, 2026-07-13 — pre-decision idea capture; NOTHING committed to build)

1. **Scanner second-order payoffs (same fusibility machinery):** (a) a token-DFA is BIDIRECTIONAL — sampling accepting paths =
   token-layer STIMULI GENERATION (duality-complete primitive; possible lever on witnessing-wall classes); (b) EXPECTED-TOKEN
   diagnostics from DFA states ("expected one of …" at rejects — a user-facing quality win beyond `furthest_position`); (c) the
   fusibility census as a STANDING grammar metric ("token-shapedness", tracked like cert coverage; flags needlessly irregular rules).
2. **Residual engine ideas (scanner-independent):** (a) ADAPTIVE/LAZY MEMOIZATION — after first-set pruning, measure whether memo
   probes still pay rent (`PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` on the bench; literature: Nez elastic packrat window, cut-operator memo elision);
   fused regions need no memo at all (DFA linear by construction); (b) TYPED/ZERO-COPY OUTPUT path in the embedding API (the ~6%
   SERDE bucket; typed visitor / borrowed carrier; contract-ADDITIVE; `regex_typed_*` probes hint RGX interest); (c) SIMD byte-class
   scanning INSIDE fused scanners later (Hyperscan/re2c playbook — an increment of the scanner rung, not a rung).
3. **⭐ THE WORKLOAD TRACE (pull hardest):** `.6` races a NUMBER without a TRACE. If RGX caches compiled matchers, PGEN parse cost
   hits only COLD patterns ⇒ the honest closure metric is consumer-relative ("PGEN ≤ X% of RGX's end-to-end pattern-compile
   pipeline") or amortized-under-recurrence. ONE real RGX workload trace (pattern arrival + recurrence histogram) converts `.6`
   from a number race into an SLO — and may show "speed is a non-issue" is closer than 99× suggests. `pgen_iteration_flow`
   vendoring = the instrument either way.
4. **Meta-lever — cheapen measurement:** every land-iff-faster verdict costs 2× ~8–13min fat-LTO builds; archive baseline binaries
   per landed rung / thin-LTO for iteration + fat-LTO only for landing measures. The campaign bottleneck is shifting from finding
   levers to EVALUATING them.
5. **Framings:** (a) Futamura — generated parser = interpreter specialized to the grammar; the scanner rung = the SECOND
   specialization (to structure classes); GLL was the opposite direction (more runtime generality) — the deep reason it refuted
   cleanly; (b) SV may win MORE than regex (multi-char tokens + SV dominates gate wall-clock ⇒ platform-velocity gain); log the
   generated-code-SIZE risk (SV artifact already 72MB — big keyword DFAs table-driven, small ones direct-coded).
6. **Char-level vs token-level (director question, tool-verified):** architecturally ALL PGEN parsers are scannerless; in PRACTICE
   other grammars' token-shaped leaves are `/.../` regex-literal terminals — SV has ~410, compiled to **323 `match_regex` sites** =
   ONE Rust-regex-engine call per token (a de-facto leaf-scanner) — while the regex parser has **0** (the REGEX-SELF-HOSTING
   directive converted all 36 `/.../` to pure char-level rules) ⇒ regex pays rule machinery PER CHARACTER, twice-compounded by the
   language itself being character-grained. **NEW INSIGHT: the derived scanner UNIFIES both leaf mechanisms and GENERALIZES
   SELF-HOSTING platform-wide** — PGEN-derived DFAs replace BOTH the char cascades (regex) AND the 323 external-engine
   `match_regex` calls (SV/VHDL/…), removing the Rust-regex crate dependency for EVERY parser (today only regex is held to that
   bar) while likely beating the general-purpose engine per call. The scanner rung = a speed lever AND the completion of the
   self-hosting doctrine.
- Engineer's suggested ordering (non-binding): 3 first (one trace can re-price everything) → scanner rung (payoffs 1a–1c compound)
  → 4 alongside as cheap infrastructure.
- **⛔ DIRECTOR STEER (2026-07-13, session #105):** register item 3 (the RGX workload trace /
  consumer-relative reframe) **SHALL NOT be considered** — "I can't control RGX, but I can control how fast PGEN runs; focus all
  attention on PGEN." NEW DATA POINT (director, RGX-side): **PGEN was ≈80% of RGX's overall compile slowness** — timestamp
  **RESOLVED (director, 2026-07-13): measured PRE-campaign, around the time RGX logged the issue report** (the ≈496µs era)
  ⇒ the landed 8.76× has ALREADY cut RGX's PGEN share ≈80%→≈31% and RGX's overall compile ≈3.4× (assuming the non-PGEN 20%
  unchanged); further PGEN speedups yield ≤≈1.46× more on RGX's pipeline (Amdahl on the ≈31% residual). The scanner rung's
  justification therefore rests on PGEN's OWN first-class speed deliverable (the north star) + that residual — consistent
  with the director's steer. Consequence: the road collapses to the PGEN-native raw-speed lever — the DERIVED-SCANNER rung.

#### F. AGREEMENT (2026-07-13, session #105) — the DERIVED-SCANNER rung is the agreed road; `.5.h` OPENED

Director, after the pull-based interface walk-through: *"the way you explained it kind of reassured me about the viability of the
process. So let's say we reached an agreement here."* The AGREED design (full detail = sections C/D/E + this interface contract):

- **Codegen (the AST pipeline = the compiler; it gains two stages, same gen-AST input):** (1) a FUSIBILITY pass (the section-D
  capability gate) marks scanner-compilable subtrees; (2) a SCANNER EMITTER builds a DFA per maximal fusible subtree (Thompson/
  subset over the rule bodies; accept states TAGGED by rule/branch; maximal munch == `longest_match`, tie-breaks encoded) and
  emits it as direct-coded `scan_*` functions INTO the same generated parser file.
- **Parse time (the communication contract):** PULL-BASED, **NO token stream, no pre-pass**. At exactly the site where the parser
  would have descended into a fused rule R, the emitted code calls `scan_R(pos) -> (accept_tag, len)` and BUILDS THE SAME
  ParseNode/folded value `parse_R` would have built from that span. Callers unchanged; AST byte-identical; context-dependent
  tokenization correct by construction (a different grammar position invokes a different scanner).
- **Two fusion increments:** (i) token-RULE fusion (each token-shaped rule body → one scan fn; also replaces the ~323 external
  `match_regex` Rust-regex-engine calls in SV etc. ⇒ platform-wide self-hosting); (ii) MERGED-CHOICE scanning (a choice site whose
  branches are all token-shaped → ONE multi-accept DFA scan replaces the N-branch tournament). Regex's win = increment (i) applied
  to its per-char cascade (char-grained "tokens" — the director's distinction, correct).
- **Untouched invariants:** `.ebnf` + return/semantic annotations (authors see NOTHING); gen-AST IR; semantic runtime/store
  (store-gated rules never fuse; adaptive boundary un-fuses on directive addition); typed JSON AST + schema (byte-identical, the
  ⛔ oracle floor); packrat memo for structural rules (unneeded inside scanners — DFA linear); the INTERPRETER stays rule-walking
  as the reference oracle; stimuli generation/duality unaffected.
- **OUT of scope (explicitly):** a batch pre-lexing mode (context-independent-token grammars only; maybe-later, capability-gated,
  only if pull-based measurably leaves wins on the table). GLL stays refuted. `.7` cache re-sequenced AFTER the rung;
  `.6` re-baseline dropped.
- **Pre-registered risks carried forward (pause-and-agree per the standing protocol):** (R-i) participation-testimony synthesis
  (cert coverage + contract gates), (R-ii) `furthest_position` parity on rejection, (R-iii) per-grammar gate breadth unknown until
  the census, (R-iv) generated-code size (SV 72MB — big keyword DFAs table-driven, small direct-coded).

#### `.5.h.1` — STEP-0 FUSIBILITY CENSUS (session #106, 2026-07-13): tools + measurements + the gate verdict

**The two read-only tools built (no codegen change, no grammar change, parser-agnostic):**

1. **`ast_pipeline <g>.ebnf --report-fusibility-census`** (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/fusibility_census.rs` + the `main.rs`
   dispatch; optional `--fusibility-census-json FILE`, `--fusibility-entry-counts F1,F2,…`, `PGEN_FUSIBILITY_DUMP_ALL=1`
   for per-rule verdicts). Classifies every rule of the UNFILTERED tree (the view codegen compiles) against the section-F
   increment-1 gate, each criterion mirroring the engine's OWN resolution (never re-derived): (1) REGULAR — acyclic
   reference closure, quantifier-only iteration (`parse_quantifier_bounds`); (2) EFFECT-FREE — no compiled runtime
   directive anywhere in the closure (`compile_semantic_runtime_annotations` + `directives_for_rule`/branch maps), no
   value constraints, no `[> …]` follow restrictions, no mid-sequence inline actions, `@transform`/`@profiles` flagged
   as distinct increment-2 classes; (3) TEXT-FOLDING — the branch value is provably the matched span: unannotated
   terminal/alternation folds, `-> $text` (`UnifiedReturnAST::MatchedText` — value = span BY CONSTRUCTION, children need
   only shape), `-> $N` passthrough with all-lookahead siblings (the `unicode_char` shape); (4) POLICY-ENCODABLE —
   `longest_match`/`ordered`/`priority_first` all DFA-encodable (maximal munch / accept-priority), `nonassoc` +
   `@deterministic_group` excluded (registry accessors `effective_rule_*`); (5) LAYOUT-CONTIGUOUS — mirrors codegen
   exactly (`match_string` skips iff `!layout.terminals`; `match_regex` skips iff `!layout.regex_tokens` minus the two
   `string_content_*` name-special-cases): multi-lexeme bodies under a skipping facet are excluded. The classifier
   separates **shape-encodable** (value-agnostic language encodability — lookahead operands and `$text` subtrees need
   only this) from **fusible** (shape + value), so the report also measures the value-building-increment candidate pool
   (`shape_only`). Maximal fusible ROOTS (the future `scan_*` sites) = fusible rules referenced by ≥1 non-fusible rule.
   Also counts the grammar's regex-literal ATOM SITES (the `match_regex`/self-hosting surface). Conservative BY DESIGN —
   every verdict is a sound under-approximation, so the ceiling never over-promises. 4 unit tests pin the
   classifier's four load-bearing shapes (terminal-chain fusible + rooted-at-top, cycles excluded, lookahead-guarded
   `$N` passthrough → lookahead tier, quantified default fold not text).

2. **`parseability_probe --parse <g> <input> --dump-rule-entry-counts-json FILE`** (`parser_registry.rs` thread-local +
   `dump_rule_entry_counts_json` helper wired into all 11 grammars' detail-parse functions; worker-thread capture for
   regex; baseline-delta so SV's stdlib preload never pollutes the measured parse). Writes
   `{grammar, accepted, total_entries, rule_entry_counts}` from the always-on monotone per-rule entry counters
   (`fetch_add` at every rule entry, successful AND backtracked — `ast_based_generator.rs:3302`) — the machine-readable
   dual of the stderr live dashboard (`--dump-rule-call-counts`), which is refresh-based and useless for a
   sub-millisecond parse. Deterministic ⇒ a re-runnable oracle.

**Cross-validations (the tools agree with every prior independent measurement):**
- `test` = **50 raw rule entries** vs the `.5.e` figure **45**: reconciled exactly — `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` reports
  45 = 24 success + 21 cached-failure MEMO TABLE entries (distinct outcomes); the counter counts raw entries including
  memo-hit re-entries (e.g. `atom` ×10). Same cascade, same ~11/char model; per-entry cost 11.79µs/50 ≈ 236ns raw.
- SV regex-literal atom sites = **322** measured vs the section-E tool-verified "~323 `match_regex` sites" (grep-based).
- regex atom sites = **0** — the REGEX-SELF-HOSTING conversion, reproduced.

parsed by the ebnf parser; `entity_only_port_decl.vhd` (vhdl); `multiple_genvar_declarations.sv` @ `sv_2017` (SV);
`macro_define_undef_guard.sv` (svpp); `3 + 4 * WIDTH` (rtl_const_expr); a minimal assign module (rtl_frontend); a
`{type:…, atom:$1}` template (return_annotation); a real `@emit_fact` line (semantic_annotation). "eliminated" counts
entries on fusible NON-root rules only — a fusible rule referenced by ANY non-fusible parent is bucketed `at roots`
(per-rule aggregate counts cannot split call paths), so the ceiling is a sound LOWER bound; the absolute per-rule-fusion
UPPER bound (every fusible + shape-only entry absorbed) for regex is 2389/(2389−1045) ≈ **1.8×**. Ceiling model: uniform
per-entry cost (~236–262ns), scan cost ≈ a terminal match (first-order 0).

**WHY the estimate fell (the architectural reading, tool-backed):** section D's "~70–80% fused entries ⇒ ~3–5×" assumed
the per-char cascade is mostly token-shaped wrappers. The census shows the opposite: on the bench, only 24.2% of regex
entries sit on increment-1-fusible rules at all, and the eliminated share is 3.5% — the cascade's bulk is the
STRUCTURAL spine (`piece`→`atom` dispatch + the per-char failing probes of `quantifier`/`zero_width`/structural-`escape`
branches), each carrying a structural return annotation (`{type: "piece", …}`) that increment (i) by definition cannot
rebuild from a span. Those entries are exactly the increment-(ii) MERGED-CHOICE surface (one multi-accept DFA over a
choice site's token-shaped branch SUBSET acting as a prefix discriminator that also kills the failing probes) — a
different, site-level construction whose payoff needs its own STEP-0 measurement before any build.

#### G.1 RE-ADJUDICATION ON THE MEASURED NUMBERS (session #107 — BOTH increments now measured; director pick pending)

The `.5.h.1b` census (results section below) closes the open measurement from section G. The complete picture:

| increment | surface | measured ceiling (8-pattern bench) |
|---|---|---|
| (i) token-RULE fusion | fusible-rule descents | ≈1.04× conservative (`.5.h.1`) |
| (ii) MERGED-CHOICE / site-DFA discrimination | discarded entries on shape-encodable rules (830 of 2389) | **≈1.53×** (`.5.h.1b`; optimistic — memo-hit entries at full weight, scans costed ~0) |
| (i)+(ii) combined ABSOLUTE bound | every encodable entry absorbed (1045 of 2389) | ≈1.78× (cross-instrument-reproduced) |
| what remains | the STRUCTURAL spine: 402 committed + 943 discarded structural entries = 56% of the bench | out of scanner-rung scope (recursive descent itself) |

**Even perfect execution of the ENTIRE agreed scanner-rung scope cannot reach 2× on the regex bench** — against

huge (74% of entries), but the killable-by-DFA share is the minority of it; the majority sits on the recursive
structural rules a DFA cannot decide exactly.

engine replacement (SV 322 / semantic_annotation 136 / vhdl 102 / rtl_frontend 47 / ebnf+svpp 30 each): a

the director's priority — and CLOSE the rung's regex-bench SPEED claim as **REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT** (both
increments). The next regex-bench speed rung candidate is `.7` (batch + parse-cache), already agreed-sequenced

#### H. THE AGREED ROAD #2 (director, 2026-07-13, session #107) — the OPTIMIZING-COMPILER ("planner") rung; `.5.i` OPENED

The post-refutation discussion converged on the architectural diagnosis and the director agreed explicitly:
*"I agree with your phrasing — in fact we just implemented 2/3 of the journey; the last is to effectively build
a compiler or planner, because what we have right now is a naive version, a transliterator. That's where things
are going to be interesting."*

**The division-of-labor contract (the agreed framing):**
- A spec language SHOULD NOT capture speed (SQL/planner, regex/engine precedents): the EBNF+annotations capture
  FUNCTIONALITY (accuracy) — they are and remain the sole semantic source of truth, byte-for-byte.
- Speed is MANUFACTURED by the compiler from what the spec already implies. PGEN today has 2/3 of the system at
  full strength: the SPEC half (EBNF+annotations) and the PROOF half (typed-AST byte-identity, cert seeds,
  equivalence gates, the interpreter as unoptimized reference). The COMPILER half is a TRANSLITERATOR — it maps
  every construct 1:1 onto maximally-defensive generic machinery (rule→guarded/memoized method, `|`→full
  tournament, `?`/`*`→snapshot-speculation) regardless of what the grammar needs at that site. That protocol is
  the measured ~236ns/entry × ~11 entries/char; 74% of bench entries are its discarded probes.
- **Hints doctrine:** the compiler DERIVES all speed decisions from grammar analysis (FIRST sets, disjointness,
  call graphs, store-gate placement). Grammar authors never think about speed. If advisory hints ever exist they
  must be provably acceptance/AST-neutral — the EBNF never becomes an implementation script.

#### `.5.i.5` P4 STEP-0 PRICING SCOUT (session #115, 2026-07-14): the `split_semantic_top_level` 6–8% is 18 evaluations/pass of GRAMMAR-CONSTANT PROSE `@constraint` strings (≈0.7–1.4µs EACH) — P4-i = codegen CONSTANT-FOLD, ceiling ≈−5–8%; P4-ii/iii/iv priced from the #6 profile

**Method (tools-first, ZERO new instrument):** generated-parser + codegen source reading joined
with the EXISTING session-#114 outcome dumps (`p3c_dumps`/`p3ci_dumps` per-rule
raw/committed/hits + `store_counters`) and the RE-PROFILE #6 inclusive-subtree numbers.

**P4-i — `@constraint` CONSTANT-FOLD AT CODEGEN (the top-named-leaf mechanism, fully mapped):**
- **WHY+WHERE (emission):** `ast_based_generator.rs` `semantic_relational_constraint_tokens`
  (:8699, policy :8655) emits, at EVERY exit of a `@constraint`-carrying rule,
  `evaluate_relational_expression(&result, "<grammar-constant string>")` + an error branch.
  The emitted evaluator RE-PARSES the string per evaluation: trim → paren-strip walk → `||`
  split (byte-walk + Vec alloc) → `&&` split (walk + alloc) → up to SIX operator once-splits
  (each a FULL walk + Vec alloc) → reference/unquote/f64 probes → `to_ascii_lowercase`
  (String alloc) → truthy fallback ⇒ ≈9 byte-walks + ≈9 allocs to conclude "prose ⇒ true".
- **THE POPULATION (dump join, per bench pass):** **18 raw evaluations** — ALL on
  `simple_escape` (email 6, anchor_complex 4, digit_sequence 3, capture_groups 3,
  character_class 1, url_simple 1; committed 16/18, hits 0). The other generated sites
  (`control_escape` ×6, `single_byte_escape` ×2, `unicode_escape`, `property_escape`,
  hex/octal/codepoint) are IDLE on this bench. Profile cap: split-subtree INCLUSIVE 6.3/8.2%
  (A/B) ⇒ measured per-eval cost ≈0.7–1.4µs — each evaluation costs ≈¼ of a whole
  `literal_simple` parse.
- **THE FOLD (all 15 sites provably constant-TRUE):** every one of the 8 distinct grammar
  strings (`grammars/regex.ebnf` `@constraint:` prose, e.g. "produces control character") is
  operator-free, `||`/`&&`-free, un-negated, NOT reference syntax (no `$`), unquoted,
  non-numeric, ∉ {true,false} ⇒ the emitted decision procedure lands in
  `semantic_truthy(non-empty prose) = true` UNCONDITIONALLY; all 15 sites carry EMPTY
  `requires` refs (`&[]`, verified 15/15); `@implies` is used NOWHERE. Codegen therefore
  classifies the constant at GENERATION time (the narrowest sound gate: no top-level
  structure ∧ not reference/quoted/numeric/boolean ⇒ constant-true) and **emits NOTHING** —
  the runtime check is dead code by construction (a constant-true check has no observable
  surface: no trace line, no store touch, an error branch that can never fire). Non-constant
  expressions keep today's runtime path unchanged. Parser-agnostic: the fold lives in the
  SHARED codegen path (any grammar's prose `@constraint` benefits; regex is today's only live
  user — semantic_annotation's one `@constraint` match is a comment).
- **FALSIFIABLE CEILING ≈ −5–8% geomean** — cap = the whole measured mechanism (6.3–8.2%
  inclusive + the small evaluator tail outside split frames); population-derived cross-check
  18 × 0.7–1.4µs ≈ 13–25µs of the ≈300µs bench sum ✓ consistent. Skew: email/anchor/digit/
  capture faster; literal/alternation untouched (0 evaluations).
- **Honest bound (recorded, out of increment scope):** the INTERPRETER does not evaluate
  `@constraint` at all (no relational machinery in `parse_harness_interpreter.rs`) — a
  PRE-EXISTING latent divergence class for a hypothetical constant-FALSE or content-dependent
  constraint (today's equivalence-gate green + all-prose-true constraints make it invisible).
  The fold does not widen it: a folded constant-true check is behaviorally identical on both
  sides. A durable closure (interpreter mirror or a constant-false lint) is a separate leaf.
- ⛔ Emission-slice requirements: the `.5.i.4` battery verbatim (land-iff-faster alternated
  5×2000 + byte-identical full oracle set + all-11 regen with per-parser diff audit + the
  dual-feature `ast_pipeline` rebuild trap).

**P4-ii — memo-stored `Value` ownership (drop-churn):** cap = `drop<RegexParser>` 5.4–5.5%
(parser teardown cascading the memo's STORED shaped `Value`s) + in-parse `MemoEntry` drops
≈1.0–1.5%. Design: stop cloning shaped values into memo entries (Rc/arena ownership across
replay). **Ceiling ≈ −4–6%; needs a design spike** (replay ownership semantics).

**P4-iii — shaped-view capture clone folding:** cap = `ParseContent::clone` inclusive
11.3–11.7% (+ `clone_subtree` overlap 12.7–14.1%). CLASS-WIDE — spread across the
`parse_piece`/`parse_atom`/`parse_regex`/`parse_entry_alternation` shaped-view capture
closures with NO dominant site ⇒ requires the value-representation design (Rc<Value>/CoW/
arena-Json), not a point fix. **The LARGEST P4 surface: ceiling ≈ −9–13%.**

**P4-iv — boundary `to_json_value` move-not-clone:** cap = inclusive 3.8–4.1% ⇒ **ceiling
≈ −3%** (the #5 "largest single site" framing is dead — RE-PROFILE #6).

**⇒ STEER (emission order within P4):** **P4-i FIRST** (clean, codegen-only, sound gate fully
verified this scout, ceiling ≈−5–8%) → re-profile → **P4-iii design spike** (largest surface)
with **P4-ii folded into the same value-ownership design**; P4-iv rides along on that design.

#### `.5.i.6` P4-i LANDED (session #115, 2026-07-14): the `@constraint` CONSTANT-FOLD — regex geomean **−12.1%** (all 5 rounds faster), ≈31µs-era → **≈27.4µs**, cumulative 496µs → ≈27.4µs ≈ **18.1×**

**THE CHANGE (codegen-only, parser-agnostic — `ast_based_generator.rs`; NO engine change, NO
grammar change):** `semantic_relational_constraint_tokens` now consults a generation-time
constant-truth gate `relational_constraint_is_provably_truthy(expr)` and, when the rule's whole
relational policy is exactly {constant-true `@constraint`, zero `@requires` refs, no `@implies`},
**emits NOTHING** — the rule-exit guard is dead code by construction (no trace line, no store
effect, an error branch that can never fire; `enforce_relational_requires(&[])` proven a pure
no-op). The gate is STRICTLY narrower than the emitted evaluator, each banned character mapping
to one evaluator feature (doc-comment carries the full mirror map): non-empty ∧ none of
`$ " ' ( ) < > = ! | &` ∧ **not a bare dotted-identifier chain** ∧ `f64` parse fails ∧ lowered ∉
{true,false,0,no,off,none,null}. Non-constant expressions keep the runtime path VERBATIM.
**Soundness near-miss caught by the full-procedure read (recorded):** `semantic_reference_syntax`
accepts `$`-less bare/dotted identifiers (`validated`, `a.b.c`) — such a "constraint" resolves
against parse content and can REJECT when unresolved, so a naive prose gate keyed only on
banned characters would have mis-folded it; the identifier-chain exclusion (mirroring
`semantic_identifier` byte-for-byte) closes it, and the truth-table test pins both directions.
Unit tests: `relational_constraint_constant_truth_gate` (8 live strings fold; 30 adversarial
shapes don't) + `constant_true_constraint_folds_to_no_emission` (emission-level pin, both
directions).

saved landed P3c-i probe `09b20e98…`; candidate = fresh fat-LTO build on the folded regen
`f5506c88…`. Per-round ratios **0.884/0.887/0.877/0.879/0.868** ⇒ geomean **0.879 = −12.1%**,
candidate faster EVERY round; best-mins 31.30µs → **27.38µs** (0.875). Per-pattern best-min
ratios MATCH the scout's population map: email_basic **0.690** (6 evals), digit_sequence
**0.737** (3 evals, small parse), url_simple 0.849, anchor_complex 0.888, capture_groups 0.921,
character_class 0.962 (1 eval, large parse); the two ZERO-evaluation patterns: alternation 0.988
(noise) and literal_simple **1.022** — the fold removes no code on literal_simple's path, so the
+2.2% (~110ns on the 5µs pattern) is fat-LTO layout jitter, the known smallest-pattern class;
geomean faster all rounds regardless. EXCEEDS the ≈−5–8% ceiling again — the ceiling capped
only the split-subtree share; the evaluator tail (lowercase/truthy/error-format machinery),
≈9-allocs/eval allocator relief (V6-class synergy), and the I-cache effect of deleting 15

**VERDICTS (the scout protocol doing its job BEFORE emission):**
- ⛔ **P4-ii (memo-stored `Value` ownership, was priced ≈−4–6%) REFUTED for the reported

- ⛔ **P4-iv (boundary move-not-clone, was ≈−3%) SUBSUMED** — the capture-idiom first copy
  becomes a ref-copy under the fold; the residual `to_json_value` deep share ≈3% is the

  composition). The **root-output drop 5.53/5.96% is an IN-window cost of DISCARDING the
  output** (`let _ =`) — only a value-representation or bench-protocol change moves it;
  protocol pinned ⇒ recorded honestly, NOT claimed by any increment.
- ✅ **P4-iii CONFIRMED with a named, codegen-only increment — the STRUCTURAL-REFERENCE
  FOLD:** in the `$1`/branch-default extraction, PRESERVE the reference instead of
  materializing — `Alternative(node) => ParseContent::Alternative(node)` (keep the wrapper),
  `Sequence(elements) [single-capture] => ParseContent::Alternative(&elements[k])`;
  `other => other.clone()` and every `@transform`/value_compare-feeding site stay VERBATIM in
  increment 1. Value-equal by definition: `to_json_value(Alternative(n)) ≡
  n.content.to_json_value()` — a value is deep-materialized ONCE per enclosing object/array
  template instead of once per level; loser-branch extraction becomes a ref copy.
  **Falsifiable ceiling ≈ −10–13%** (9.05–11.66 body deep-clones + ≈1–2 shallow
  `ParseContent::clone` overhead + ≈0.3–0.5 churn drops; the memo/arena/parser teardown
  shrink is a metric-invisible bonus, NOT claimed). Falsifiers: a battery divergence, or a
  measured delta below the ±1–3% noise floor.

**Soundness obligations (pre-emission inventory; the ⛔ battery adjudicates):** (i) every
shaped-view consumer that matches `ParseContent::Json` must treat `Alternative(→Json)`
identically — property access / `.len` / value_compare / `@transform` coercion / `@emit_fact`
payload resolution (`unified_semantic_ast.rs` already recurses `Alternative` at :353; the :139
comment records annotation content flowing through `Alternative` as a handled case); (ii) NO
gate surface may serialize the raw node tree of a shaped grammar (byte-identity is at
`ast_json` level — grep for raw `ParseNode` serde serialization in registry/dump paths; the
retired rtl_frontend raw-envelope is the precedent); (iii) memo replay is
representation-agnostic (content cloned as-is; `Alternative` refs borrow the per-parse arena,
same lifetime as the per-parse memo); (iv) the RAW channel (`semantic_raw_content`) is
untouched. The interpreter needs NO mirror change for byte-identity (equivalence/combinator/
semantic gates compare converted `ast_json`, not internal representation).

**Research grounding (the design is a worked mapping, not trial-and-revert):** the fold is
**deforestation** of the shaped-value pipeline — eliminating intermediate tree
materialization between producer (child shaping) and consumer (parent template) [Wadler,
"Deforestation: transforming programs to eliminate trees", TCS 1990]; the arena node refs
already provide the shared immutable tree layer that red-green syntax trees use for subtree
reuse [Roslyn red-green trees; rust-analyzer Rowan — `Alternative(&node)` is the "projection
as reference" idiom]. The heavier endpoints surveyed and NOT taken, with reasons: arena/tape
value representation [simdjson — Langdale & Lemire, "Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second",
VLDB J. 2019] and `Rc<Value>`/CoW at content boundaries — both attack whole-content clone +
teardown surfaces that are now measured mostly POST-window here, at engine-wide blast radius;
lazy boundary values [serde_json `RawValue` precedent] break the "shaped values readable
mid-parse" contract (shaped-view `$refs`, value_compare). Re-visit only if the fold
underdelivers.

**Closure math:** ceiling ≈27.4µs → ≈24µs ≈ 24× from the COLD ≤1µs bar — P4 stays a finisher
pass; the deep-specialization planner extensions remain ON-ROAD after P4 (director,
2026-07-13). Frontier = the P4-iii fold EMISSION under the leaf's ⛔ HARD CONSTRAINT battery.

**EMISSION DESIGN REFINEMENT (session #116, pre-code — obligation (ii) executed and it
CHANGED the mechanism):** `parse_node_to_json` (`parser_registry.rs:1549`) serde-serializes
the ENTIRE `ParseNode` tree with the DERIVED externally-tagged `ParseContent` encoding — an
`Alternative` wrapper would be byte-VISIBLE in every dump (`{"Alternative": {...}}` where
today the unwrap emits `{"Json": ...}`), so the naive Alternative-preserving fold FAILS the
byte-identity battery by construction. REFINED MECHANISM: a new variant
**`ParseContent::JsonRef(&'input serde_json::Value)`** — a reference INTO the arena-lived
child node's owned `Json` value — with **`#[serde(rename = "Json")]`**, so it serializes
BYTE-IDENTICALLY to `Json`; `clone` = ref copy (O(1)); `to_json_value` deep-copies only at
true materialization sites. The extraction fold emits `Json(v) → JsonRef(v)` /
`JsonRef(v) → JsonRef(v)` / `other → other.clone()` at every `$N`/passthrough extraction
site (one shared helper in `ast_return_transform.rs`, no drift). Object/array-template
captures also drop from TWO deep copies (extract-clone + `to_json_value` re-clone) to ONE.
Twin-arm inventory (the mirror rule — `JsonRef` twins wherever `Json` is pattern-NAMED,
shared wildcard routing otherwise, so routing parity is inductive): engine sites in
`unified_return_ast.rs` (:800/:2007/:2041/:2099/:2780), `unified_semantic_ast.rs`
(:128/:352), `semantic_runtime.rs` (:5043), `ast_shape_contract.rs` (:138/:655),
`grammar_wellformedness.rs` (:2109), `parser_registry.rs`, `parser_hooks/regex.rs`,
`ebnf_dual_run_diff.rs` (:75), `rtl_frontend_generated_contract_probe.rs`,
`parse_harness_interpreter.rs` (:1729/:1851/:3161 — the interpreter never CONSTRUCTS
`JsonRef`; twins for routing parity), + the emitted-template sites in
`ast_based_generator.rs` (:6839/:6992/:7588) and `ast_return_transform.rs`
(`parse_content_to_string` — ⚠️ the caught divergence: `Json(String)` unquotes, a wildcard
fallback would re-quote — and `generate_array_access`'s Json arm). Bootstrap safety BY
CONSTRUCTION: emitted matches all carry wildcards, so the previous-generation parsers
compile against the extended enum (no `.5.i.1.t1`-class chicken-and-egg). Derived
`PartialEq` treats `Json`≠`JsonRef` — no behavioral content-equality use exists in engine
paths (grep: only test-string comparisons); noted, not load-bearing.

**WHY the ceiling failed — the new named class:** the #7 profile's 9.05–11.66 % in-window
deep-clone share is a share of ALL sampled CPU across steady-state iterations; the campaign
metric is geomean-of-MINS. Allocator-churn cost (clone+drop traffic) concentrates in
above-min iterations (allocator slow paths, cache misses); the min-iteration barely contains
it, so removing the mechanism barely moves the metric. Retroactive cross-check that CONFIRMS
the class: P4-i (−12.1 % on a 6–8 % surface) and P3c-i (−11.2 % on a ≈9 % surface) EXCEEDED
their ceilings because their surfaces were FIXED per-parse compute (expression re-parsing,
protocol calls) fully present in every iteration incl. the min; P4-iii's surface was almost
pure allocator traffic. ⇒ Scout discipline amendment (recorded for every future pricing):
price a ceiling against the metric's OWN basis — a sampled-share ceiling is only valid for
fixed-compute mechanisms; alloc-churn surfaces need a min-basis estimate (or an explicit
`mean` metric decision by the director).

#### `.5.i.7` D0 EMISSION DESIGN (session #118, 2026-07-14 — recorded BEFORE emission; scope decisions on the STEP-0 numbers)

**The increment (analysis-only, engine tier — justified per the fix hierarchy: no grammar or
annotation can express FIRST-byte derivation; the LANDED `.5.c.2` prune and P2 dispatch amplify
automatically at regen with zero new emission machinery):**

1. **`FirstSetSummary` carrier extension** (`first_set.rs`): three new fields —
   `first_bytes: BTreeSet<u8>` (first bytes contributed by NON-quoted origins: regex-token
   terminals with derivable prefixes + native builtin matchers; disjoint carrier from
   `terminals`, so the validator's string-keyed lints are byte-stable by construction),
   `regex_token_derived: bool` (any of `first_bytes` came from a `/regex/` terminal — such bytes
   are sound for prune/dispatch ONLY when regex tokens do not skip leading layout), and
   `byte_decided: bool` (match success at any position ⟺ next byte ∈ the summary's exact byte
   set — the license for negative-lookahead subtraction).
2. **The `"regex"` arm derives first bytes from the pattern's HIR** (`regex-syntax` 0.8, already
   a dependency — the SAME dialect `match_regex`'s `regex::Regex::new` compiles): classes
   (incl. negated — HIR pre-resolves negation) map char ranges to UTF-8 lead-byte bands
   (monotonic within each 1/2/3/4-byte band ⇒ contiguous lead ranges), literals contribute
   their first byte, concat unions while nullable, alternation unions, `min=0` repetition ⇒
   nullable, zero-width `Look`s are prefix-transparent. Soundness anchor: `match_regex` is
   ANCHORED (`\A(?:…)`, PARSE-TERMINATION.7.1) ⇒ a regex terminal's match first byte IS the
   byte at the parse position. The existing exact `find("")` nullability stays authoritative.
   Derivation failure ⇒ the current `unresolved: true` (behavior-preserving fallback).
   `byte_decided` for a regex token = single ASCII-only class / single-byte literal (in-set ⇒
   definite match), and only when non-nullable.
3. **Native builtins resolve after a grammar-tree miss** (mirroring codegen's
   `NATIVE_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE_BUILTINS` precedence — grammar definition wins):
   `builtin_ascii_char` ⇒ `{0x00–0x7F}` byte-decided (`is_ascii()` = first-byte-exact);
   `builtin_any_char` ⇒ all UTF-8 lead bytes `{0x00–0x7F, 0xC2–0xF4}` byte-decided (at a char
   boundary of a valid `&str` the next byte is always a lead byte and the match succeeds);
   `true`/`false` ⇒ nullable zero-width always-succeed (resolved, never prunable);
   `semantic_annotation` stays UNRESOLVED (its native matcher skips layout first ⇒ first-byte
   peeking unsound).
4. **Exact negative-lookahead subtraction in Sequence** — the mechanism that resolves the
   scout's central case `unicode_char := !builtin_ascii_char builtin_any_char` to the
   non-ASCII lead bytes: every FIRST contribution of a sequence occurs AT the sequence's start
   position, and `!X` with X byte-decided fails there EXACTLY on X's byte set, so
   FIRST(rest) − bytes(X) is exact-sound (subtraction requires the lookahead element
   byte-decided + resolved + non-nullable; an over-approximated set must never be subtracted).
   The lookahead's own junk `terminals` still union into the summary (validator byte-stability);
   only its `first_bytes` are withheld and the exclusion set applied to later contributions.
5. **Consumer trust gate**: `branch_dispatch_first_bytes` (the SHARED P2 predicate) gains a
   `trust_regex_token_bytes` parameter — codegen passes `layout_sensitivity().regex_tokens`,
   the census passes its compiled `layout.regex_tokens`; a summary with
   `regex_token_derived && !trust` is treated as unresolved (never "builtin-bytes-only" — that
   would under-approximate). The `.5.c.2` prune guard applies the same gate and now unions
   `summary.first_bytes` with the quoted-terminal first bytes. Builtin-derived bytes need no
   gate (the native matchers never skip layout).
6. **Emission/analysis pattern alignment**: the `first_set_grammar_tree` snapshot choke point
   now rewrites every regex atom through `effective_regex_pattern(rule, raw)` so the analysis
   sees EXACTLY the pattern the emitted `match_regex` will compile (`@token_class`/`@charset`/
   explicit-pattern steering + the semantic_annotation `identifier_literal` special case).
   Idempotent for the P1a inline-emission path (steering returns its replacement regardless of
   input; the special case keys on the RAW spelling) ⇒ inline bodies emit byte-identically.
   HONEST BOUND: the census analyzes the raw tree (no steering applied) — drift is currently ∅
   (no tracked grammar uses token steering; the sole live special case is first-byte-equivalent)
   and census is diagnostic-only; recorded here rather than silently ignored.

**Blast radius (measured before emission):** only `regex.ebnf` is `@whitespace_sensitive: true`
(FULL — terminals sensitive ⇒ emit gate ON); `systemverilog_preprocessor.ebnf` is
`{ regex_tokens: true }` (terminals INsensitive ⇒ emit gate OFF). ⇒ **exactly ONE parser may
change at regen: `regex_parser.rs`; the other 10 generated artifacts must be byte-identical**
(pre-regen sha256 snapshot taken: regex `83a68f23…` + 10 pins in the session scratchpad).
Interpreter untouched (prune/dispatch cannot change verdict/AST — the equivalence gate proves
it). ⛔ HARD CONSTRAINT verbatim (the `.5.i.6` battery): land iff measured faster on fat-LTO
alternated 5×2000 geomean-of-mins both sides rebuilt fresh, + byte-identical ASTs under the
full oracle battery; counters are EXPECTED to change (discard kills are the mechanism — the
scout's 8/8 outcome-dump pins are superseded at land, AST pins are not).
